profiles.summary: The official node still gives the specified result for all 185,529 opcode vectors, for 21,759 new jump targets into and around push data, and for the PoolManager scripts, and the whole mined swap history of the PoolManager (2,284 swaps, 702 at negative ticks) satisfies the source's math. The two public replay clients pin older libraries than OPCODES.md records (revm 19.2.0 with ruint 1.15.0, and a revm 29.0.1 fork with ruint 1.16.0), and no fix released since then changes an arithmetic, jump or memory result. The official endpoint's eth_call path differs from block execution in two observed ways that do not touch the opcodes the PoolManager uses.

deltas.delta: Rerun on the official endpoint (web3_clientVersion 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet', head 52,117,929 on 2026-11-24): battery.py 99,985 of 99,985 vectors and targeted.py 85,544 of 85,544 vectors with no mismatch; pmdiff.py identical on 250 of 250 scripts; pmdiff2.py identical on 299 of 300. The one differing script (189, native, dynamic fee) returns nothing at 25 million gas and is identical to Ethereum at 30 million gas, so it is the known gas case. Files cycles/010/hyperevm.work/out/battery.json, targeted.json, pmdiff.json, pmdiff2.json, pmdiff2_explain189.json.
deltas.source: rpc https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call with state override, results in research/network-risk/cycles/010/hyperevm.work/out/

deltas.delta: New live jump destination probe (cycles/010/hyperevm.work/jdlive.py): 300 generated layouts of 300 to 3,000 bytes with PUSH1 to PUSH32 whose data holds 0x5b followed by a return sequence, fillers at every phase across 16, 32 and 64 byte borders, and truncated trailing PUSH32. 21,759 targets: 1,324 real JUMPDESTs succeed, and 6,935 targets on 0x5b inside push data, 12,000 other bytes and 1,500 offsets at or past the end of code all fail, as specified. No mismatch.

Library versions of the public replay clients, read from their lock files on 2026-11-24. hyper-evm-sync (main) pins revm 19.2.0, revm-interpreter 15.2.0, revm-primitives 15.2.0, ruint 1.15.0, alloy-primitives 0.8.25, SpecId CANCUN. nanoreth (master, Cargo.toml unchanged since cycle 7) patches every revm crate to hl-archive-node/revm at fdf9b16, which is revm 29.0.1 / interpreter 25.0.3 plus a backport of revm PR 3805 that only changes the inspector's SELFDESTRUCT callback, with ruint 1.16.0 and alloy-primitives 1.3.1. Neither pins ruint 1.21.0.

ruint fixes after 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 that could matter for EVM results: 1.16.0 #476 (limb overflow check in shifts), 1.20.0 #603 (overflow flag of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr, and byte()), 1.21.1 or later #681 (mul_mod with equal top limbs, introduced in 1.21.0). The 1.15.0 source of overflowing_shl, overflowing_shr and arithmetic_shr computes the correct value and only the overflow flag is affected, revm clamps shift and byte indices to below 256 and 32 before calling ruint, and byte() at 1.16.0 indexes the little endian slice directly. revm-interpreter fixes after 15.2.0 are gas, SELFDESTRUCT cold load, BLOCKHASH range, memory limit errors and inspector changes; none corrects an arithmetic, jump or memory result.

The official endpoint answers every block tag with the latest state (hyperliquid-dex/node issue 158, open). Confirmed on 2026-11-24: eth_getCode of the PoolManager returns its 24,009 bytes at block 0x1 and at block 0x5000000 (31.8 million blocks above the head), while the archive client rpc.purroofgroup.com returns 0x at block 0x1. It also does not serve debug_traceCall (Method not found). A public proof of concept reports that block.timestamp read in eth_call on this endpoint is one second below the header timestamp of the same block. The PoolManager bytecode reads no block field (OPCODES.md:146), so neither changes what it computes; both mean that any HyperEVM reading pinned to a past block through the official endpoint describes the head.

Whole mined history, read from the archive client: 3,126 PoolManager Swap and ModifyLiquidity logs from block 46,002,270 to 52,117,384. All 2,284 swaps satisfy the tick relation (2,284 exact, 0 boundary, 0 mismatch). 702 swaps end at a negative tick, the lowest at -403,562; 8 end within 2^16 of MAX_TICK, the highest at 887,271. Of 2,102 pairs, 1,921 match a single-step outcome to the unit (1,812 exact input, 32 exact output, 77 reaching the target), 181 took several steps and 0 are unexplained. The newest 25 multi-step swaps replay to the unit (up to 4 steps) from storage at their block on the archive client.
deltas.source: rpc https://rpc.purroofgroup.com eth_getLogs and eth_getStorageAt, research/network-risk/cycles/010/hyperevm.work/out/swaps_all.json and replay_archive.json

deltas.delta: Step trace of the archive client (reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31, the revm 29.0.1 fork) against the reference interpreter tools/opdiff/pyevm.py: 22 PoolManager scripts, 772,941 steps, identical in depth, program counter, opcode and the top four stack words; 8 heavy scripts skipped. This covers the replay client, not the validator.

profiles.summary: Lead L-602 is answered: no multi-bit fold of storage or transient slot keys on the official node, and committed PoolManager storage of 105 pools satisfies the cross-slot invariants. Nothing new about transaction boundaries.

deltas.delta: slotalias.py and slotalias_transient.py on the official node: 22 base slots, 5,837 alias reads each for SSTORE/SLOAD and TSTORE/TLOAD (every XOR mask 1 to 255, neighbours across a 128 boundary, the high bits 249 to 255, truncated page indices); no alias read returned a nonzero word.

invariants.py found no PoolManager log in its 5,439 block window, so invariants_pools.py ran the same checks over the 344 pool ids of cycle 7: 105 pools whose key the PositionManager returns, 180 initialized ticks, 44,740 bitmap words, 21 pools at a negative tick, 88 extsload against eth_getStorageAt comparisons (3 near a page edge); 0 violations of I1 to I4.

profiles.summary: Nothing new for gas, the native currency or token contracts this cycle; the focus was the interpreter. The only gas effect seen again is that one heavy script needs more than 25 million gas, which the 30 million gas cap of a simulated call covers.

Nothing new about precompiles or system contracts. The incidents of the last two years that name HyperEVM are application faults (oracle integrations, a vault role) and do not involve a precompile or system contract acting for the PoolManager.

cleared.check: Arithmetic, comparison, shift, byte, sign extension, MULMOD, ADDMOD, KECCAK256, MCOPY, CALLDATALOAD and JUMPI on the official node at head 52,117,929: rerun of battery.py and targeted.py for chain 999.
cleared.result: 185,529 of 185,529 vectors give the specified word. The values that TickMath (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:57-114 and 121-237), BitMath (src/libraries/BitMath.sol:12, 31), FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-48, 109-112) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:16-47) take from these opcodes are therefore what the source text computes.

cleared.check: Same PoolManager bytecode and state, compared with Ethereum: rerun of pmdiff.py (250 scripts) and pmdiff2.py (300 scripts) for chain 999.
cleared.result: pmdiff identical on 250 of 250. pmdiff2 identical on 299 of 300; script 189 returns no record at 25 million gas on HyperEVM and is byte identical to Ethereum at 30 million gas, so the difference is gas only, as recorded in opcodes/pmdiff2-gas.json.

cleared.check: Jump destination analysis of the official node: does a jump to 0x5b inside push data, to any non JUMPDEST byte or past the end of code fail, and does a jump to every real JUMPDEST succeed, across 16, 32 and 64 byte borders and with a truncated trailing PUSH32?
cleared.result: 21,759 targets over 300 layouts, no mismatch. The PoolManager bytecode has 29 bytes of value 0x5b in push data (OPCODES.md:146); a node that accepted them would change control flow, and the probe shows this node does not.

cleared.check: Library versions of the public replay clients against the fixes released since: hyper-evm-sync with revm 19.2.0 and ruint 1.15.0, nanoreth with the hl-archive-node revm 29.0.1 fork and ruint 1.16.0.
cleared.result: No ruint fix after 1.15.0 changes a value that revm returns for an opcode: #476 and #603 concern overflow flags and checked variants, revm clamps shift and byte indices first, and the shift functions of 1.15.0 compute the right value (read in src/bits.rs at tag v1.15.0). The faulty mul_mod of 1.21.0 is in neither client. revm-interpreter fixes after 15.2.0 change gas, SELFDESTRUCT cold load, BLOCKHASH and error codes only. The hl-archive-node fork differs from revm 29.0.1 by an inspector fix that does not touch execution (comment in nanoreth Cargo.toml).

cleared.check: Do the swaps that HyperEVM blocks executed, over the whole history of the PoolManager, follow the source's math, including negative ticks and ticks near the price limits?
cleared.result: 2,284 swaps from block 46,002,270 to 52,117,384 all satisfy the tick relation of getTickAtSqrtPrice and Pool.swap (src/libraries/Pool.sol:430-431); 702 are at negative ticks, which exercise SAR, SIGNEXTEND and SDIV on negative values in TickBitmap.compress and TickMath; 8 are within 2^16 of MAX_TICK. 1,921 of 2,102 pairs match one step of SwapMath.computeSwapStep to the unit, none is unexplained, and the 25 newest multi-step swaps replay to the unit from storage at their block. These are results of the closed validator.

cleared.check: Step trace of the archive client against the reference interpreter for the PoolManager scripts.
cleared.result: 22 scripts, 772,941 steps identical; 8 skipped as heavy. The archive client verifies headers against the validator's blocks, so a divergence would have stopped it; it is not the validator.

cleared.check: The official endpoint's eth_call path differs from block execution: block tags are ignored (node issue 158) and block.timestamp in eth_call is reported one second below the header. Does either change what the PoolManager computes or decides?
cleared.result: No. The bytecode has no TIMESTAMP, NUMBER or other block field instruction (OPCODES.md:146) and core has no dependence on block time (ASSUMPTIONS.md A10). Funds are decided by block execution, which the mined swaps cover. The effect is on evidence and integrations: a quote or balance read 'at block N' from this endpoint is the head state.

cleared.check: Lead L-602: multi-bit folding of persistent and transient slot keys (slotalias.py, slotalias_transient.py) on the official node.
cleared.result: 22 bases, 5,837 alias reads each, no nonzero read. The delta slots of CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39), the lock and count slots, and the keccak slots of pool state are therefore separate on this node.

cleared.check: Lead L-602: cross-slot invariants of committed PoolManager storage (invariants.py I1 to I4) over the pool ids of cycle 7.
cleared.result: 105 pools, 180 initialized ticks, 44,740 bitmap words, 88 extsload against eth_getStorageAt comparisons, no violation; 239 pools were skipped because the PositionManager returns no key for them. Layout from src/libraries/StateLibrary.sol:11-28.

cleared.check: Known weaknesses of the last two years that name HyperEVM: Prime oracle replay of 16 September 2026, Lazy Summer guardian role on HyperEVM in July 2026, PaperTrade BBO pricing of October 2026, the JELLY event of March 2025, Chainstack's stale eth_call incident of 20 October 2026, node issue 183 (EVM checkpoints never pruned), the block timestamp proof of concept, and node issue 158.
cleared.result: None is an execution client, precompile or system contract fault that an ordinary account could use against PoolManager funds. The first four are application or HyperCore market events; the Chainstack incident and issues 158 and 183 affect RPC answers or node disk only; the timestamp discrepancy is in the eth_call path and the PoolManager reads no block field.

leads.question: Which revm and ruint versions does hl-node, the closed validator, link? hl-visor (8,305,392 bytes, commit c6b742f0 of 2026-09-09) builds from vendored crates under z_vendor without version strings, and the hl-node binary path on binaries.hyperliquid.xyz is not public (403). A version list or a statement from Hyperliquid would settle whether a validator upgrade could bring in ruint 1.21.0 or a later rewrite.
leads.why: Every HyperEVM arithmetic clearance rests on the official endpoint and on mined results; the library under the validator is known only by inference from the replay clients.

leadResults.answer: For HyperEVM: slotalias.py and slotalias_transient.py on the official node, 22 bases with 5,837 alias reads each, found no fold of persistent or transient slot keys. invariants.py found no log in its recent window, so the same checks ran over the 344 pool ids of cycle 7: 105 pools, 180 initialized ticks, 44,740 bitmap words and 88 extsload against eth_getStorageAt comparisons, with no violation of I1 to I4. Files in cycles/010/hyperevm.work/out/.

The whole Swap history of 0x12D4Fd9C5DeDd00ab8a0bCe2CF0167bbf94b6B1F was read from the archive client: 2,284 swaps from block 46,002,270 to 52,117,384, all passing the tick relation, 702 at negative ticks (lowest -403,562), 8 within 2^16 of MAX_TICK (highest 887,271), none within 2^16 of MIN_TICK. 1,921 of 2,102 pairs match one step to the unit, 181 are multi-step, 0 unexplained, and the 25 newest multi-step swaps replay to the unit. The replay had to read state from the archive client because the official endpoint ignores block tags.
